families.name: Johnson 1892
families.description: An ornamental display face with rounded strokes, knob-ended curls, and an irregular rhythm.
families.observed: A–Z, a–z and 0–9 from the 1892 patent and period foundry specimens. Larger impressions inform title-critical forms.
families.reconstructed: Punctuation and symbols are newly drawn companions. Spacing is adapted for digital use.

families.name: Nero 1888
families.description: A condensed, chiseled display face with pointed terminals, deep notches, and dramatic descenders.
families.observed: Capitals A C D E F G H I K L M N O P R S T U V W; lowercase a c d e f g h i l m n o p r s t u v x y; numerals 0–9.
families.reconstructed: B J Q X Y Z and b j k q w z; modern punctuation, symbols, accented extensions and ligatures. Reconstructed forms follow the observed stroke vocabulary.

sources.title: John Ryan Foundry, Latest and Standard Faces in Type (1894), p. 135
sources.rights: US publication from 1894, beyond the maximum copyright term; scan supplied with the revival as public domain

revival.notes: Historical impressions are cleaned and harmonised into one display master. Reconstructed characters are informed by the observed letters. The j and jcircumflex were refined with a continuous stem and left-turning descender; see their editable glyph files and comparison proof.

families.name: Quaint Gothic 1894
families.designer: Unidentified in the consulted historical specimen
families.description: Contrasting sans-serif capitals with narrow hairlines and long descending strokes, revived from Ryan’s 1894 specimen.
families.observed: Capitals A–P and R–Y; figures 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 9 and dollar sign on page 148. The 24–48-point impressions anchor the master; smaller impressions supply B, J, K, M, P and X.
families.reconstructed: Q and Z; figures 0, 3, 7 and 8; punctuation and remaining symbols. Lowercase input aliases capitals, as this historical specimen shows a capitals-only face. Spacing, kerning and harmonisation between optical sizes are new. The 1894 suffix dates the source, not a claimed first release.

sources.title: John Ryan Foundry, Latest and Standard Faces in Type (September 1894), p. 148
sources.rights: 1894 US publication, beyond the 95-year maximum term. Library of Congress scan; Archive metadata states that the Library of Congress is unaware of copyright restrictions. Metadata evidence retained in reference/ryan-rights.json.

revival.notes: See source/METHOD.md and source/tracing.json for reproducible crop selection, cleanup, scaling and companion drawings. No modern font outlines were used.

families.name: Trinal 1888
families.description: Curled Victorian capitals with fine serifs, open bowls, and looping terminals, based on Trinal’s larger sizes.
families.observed: A–Z, 0–9 and ampersand, from the 1888 patent and named 1888/1894 specimens. The 24-point letters anchor the revival; documented 18- and 36-point impressions and the patent supply missing forms. K, Q, W, Z, 0, 6 and 7 are redrawn to repair damaged or rough patent impressions.
families.reconstructed: Modern punctuation and symbols are newly drawn companions. Lowercase input aliases the capitals; this is a capitals-only display face. Spacing, kerning and harmonisation between optical sizes are new. The separate swash initial alphabet and small-size variants are not included.
